desc: Core reduction: M_i=max(X,Y,Z), sort desc, take top 2K as set S with value V, color each selected item by its argmax coordinate.
All-even parity fast path: output V directly.

Build candidate ops (recolor {a->b} and swap {remove selected a, add unselected colored b}); find min single-op for mask O and min disjoint 2-op pair for the other two masks; answer = V - min(single, pair).

Verify the <=2-op optimum bound: any op multiset with parity mask O contains a 1- or 2-element sub-multiset with xor O (masks A=(0,1),B=(0,2),C=(1,2); A^B=C, A^C=B, B^C=A); ops are item-disjoint and have nonneg loss, so the extracted op(s) yield a valid configuration with loss <= the original, proving an optimal solution uses at most two ops.

Verify top-6 per-pool pruning is exact: each op consumes at most one selected and one unselected item, so the best partner disjoint from a fixed op lies within the top-2 (hence top-6) of each pool; disjoint-pair loop over generated candidates therefore attains the true minimum.

Hand-check edge/tricky cases: sample1 (V=15, single swap loss 3 -> 12), sample2 (both even -> 209, 333), and A=(10,0,0),B=(0,10,0),C=(0,0,10),D=(5,5,9),K=1 (conflicting pair (A,C)/(B,C) forces loss 1 -> 19).
Complexity/limits: O(N log N) per case (sort + linear scans), O(1) op tables; handles sum N<=1e5, T<=1000, 2K=N (empty unsel), N=2, and values up to 1e9 (Python big ints).
